why: Twelve trade titles earning $1 million to $27 million each, with 5 to 62 editorial staff, gives revenue per editorial head of roughly $150,000 to $450,000, which is believable for a trade publisher.

Wet dog food at $5.00 to $5.50 per kg ($2.20 for a 400g can, $4.00 for an 800g can) in trays of 12, with a 1,000-can discount threshold, is believable wholesale pricing, and a 60-tray order is large but possible.
An ice cream chain comparing cities on scoops per person, scoop weight, cost and price per scoop is a believable premise, and no figures are given that could be implausible.
All four score pies add to 100%, and 1,120 respondents being 14% of North customers implies about 8,000 customers, which is believable for a regional car rental business.
First-year profit of $0.80 to $18 per user against 90-day order values of $36 to $243 and average orders of about $26 to $31 is believable for a food delivery app.
Roasted beans at $21 to $24 per kg wholesale ($6 for a 250g bag, $10.50 for a 500g bag) in cases of 30, with orders of 6 cases (180 bags) from a grocery store, are believable.
The cost lines sit inside each series' total ($40,300 of $47,000 for science, $19,700 of $27,000 for history), and editor pay of $34 an hour and proofreader pay of $14 an hour are believable.
A regional motoring club whose round-the-clock patrols help 58,000 drivers a year, about 160 a day, is believable.

Profit equals revenue minus costs in both columns, and about 21 collection days, 1.2 to 1.3 million bins and about $5 million in revenue a month (around $3.90 per bin) are believable for a waste collector serving a group of towns.

Half-year revenues of $733 million to $792 million agree with 'over $1.4 billion' a year, revenue of about $40,000 per cleaner across 38,000 cleaners is believable, and the margin index gives annual profits that fall each year.
